Oracle cut ~20,000 jobs globally — the largest layoff in company history — explicitly to fund AI data center buildout. Freed $8-10B/year for AI infrastructure capex.
Verizon cut ~15,000 jobs as part of restructuring explicitly framed around the "age of AI." CEO cited automation and AI as central to the company's future operating model.
Cognizant cut 12,000-15,000 jobs under "Project Leap" — explicitly built around replacing legacy IT support roles with AI-powered service delivery.
Panasonic announced ~10,000 job cuts globally as part of cost restructuring and technology consolidation.

UPS cut an additional 36,000 operations jobs in 2025 as it pivoted to AI-powered route planning, robotics, and automated sorting. Combined with 12,000 management cuts in Jan 2024, total reduction exceeded 48,000.
Walmart cut ~8,500 corporate and supply chain roles in early 2026 as automation and AI-driven logistics reduced headcount needs across distribution centers and back-office functions.

Novo Nordisk cut 9,000 jobs (~11% of global workforce) due to GLP-1 market competition from Eli Lilly. No AI or automation cited as a reason. Included as part of broader white-collar workforce evisceration trend.

Coinbase cut ~700 employees (14% of workforce). CEO Brian Armstrong explicitly cited AI acceleration as the driver — restructuring to 'AI-native pods' where single employees direct AI agents handling engineering, design, and product. 'Pure managers' replaced with 'player-coaches.' One of the clearest executive attributions of layoffs directly to AI transformation.
